transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood, AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood, SE), Luis Moreno (Stratus IO, CTO), Rina Kapoor (Stratus IO, ML Eng), Ben Chu (Stratus IO, SRE)

Summary: quick POC scoping focused on latency/throughput SLOs for an interactive assistant use case. Discussed TTFT vs TPOT definitions, p95/p99 targets, benchmark plan (synthetic + e2e), workload sizing, and logistics (network, sample data, timelines).

Topics:
- POC goals / success criteria
- Workload sizing (tokens/day, concurrency)
- Latency metrics: TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets
- Measurement plan: synthetic vs end-to-end, warm vs cold, KV cache considerations
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros, i'm maya from redwood, our se ethan is with me.
[00:12] Luis: hi, luis here, we run the product org at stratus, rina and ben are here to scope the p o c.
[00:20] Rina: hey all, excited, we've been looking at latency for our chat assistant, want to make sure we can hit interactive snappy responses.
[00:30] Ethan: great, so we want to align on definitions first — we typically split latency into TTFT, time to first token, and TPOT, time per token. does that match your mental model?
[00:42] Rina: yes, though we also care abt total end-to-end for users, but separation is useful.
[00:48] Ben: and we need p95 and p99 targets, and also throughput targets so the backend won't queue up under peak.

[01:10] Ethan: ok so for interactive assistant scenarios, we commonly target TTFT p95 around 250-350ms and p99 < 600-800ms depending on model size; TPOT p95 around 30-60ms for small-medium models and higher for L larger ones. those are ballpark, we should pick numbers for your POC.
[01:35] Luis: our initial ask is strict — TTFT p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 700ms, and sustain 50 concurrent users with average 2 tokens/sec output (roughly 100 tokens per response). is that reasonable?
[01:52] Maya: that's a good starting point. couple clarifications: 50 concurrent users, is that steady or peak? and what's your prompt length distribution?
[02:05] Rina: peak bursts are what we care about, steady is lower. prompts average 80 tokens in, 100 tokens out on average, some up to 500 for long context.

[02:30] Ethan: ok so workload sizing summary — avg in 80 tokens, out 100 tokens, concurrency 50 peak, bursts up to 150 concurrent in 60s windows. tokens/day estimate?
[02:45] Luis: roughly 2M tokens/day across all users, but critical is the 30-minute peak windows where latency matters.

[03:00] Ethan: for the measurement plan we'll run both: 1) synthetic inference-only benchmarks to measure raw TTFT and TPOT on pinned models/configs, 2) end-to-end tests through your app stack to capture network and extra processing. We'll capture cold start, warm, and cached KV performance.
[03:20] Rina: good, please note our infra uses an initial prefix cache for common prompts, so caching behavior matters.

[03:35] Maya: noted. also we'll want to test different model variants and quantization profiles — e.g., fp16 vs int8 — because TPOT changes with quantization.
[03:48] Ben: question on metrics collection — do you expose per-request timing? we need p95/p99 split by route and by model version.
[03:58] Ethan: yes, redwood console exposes token-level and request-level traces; we'll provide a benchmark payload that outputs the raw timings and an aggregated csv. small note: auto transcription sometimes calls it the 'redhood console' in notes ha.

[04:20] Luis: about success criteria: beyond TTFT p95/p99 we want a throughput SLO: sustain 20 rps with 95% of requests meeting TTFT target during peaks. also we want degradation policy — fallback to smaller model if we can't meet latency.
[04:40] Maya: makes sense. for the POC we propose hard success criteria: TTFT p95 <= 350ms, TTFT p99 <= 700ms, TPOT p95 <= 60ms. Throughput: sustain 20 rps with p95 TTFT target during a 5 minute peak window. these numbers are a mix of conservative and achievable for gen-2 medium models on dedicated instances.
[05:05] Rina: can you map those to specific infra? like what instance/gpu config you'll use for the baseline?
[05:14] Ethan: baseline we'll run on a 4xA10-style pool (equivalent to our dedicated small cluster), with optimized kernels and continuous batching disabled for pure low-latency run; we can also test batched throughput cases. we'll include a configuration matrix in the runbook.

[05:35] Ben: what about TTFT definition — are we measuring at client side or server side? network latency could be substantial.
[05:43] Maya: we'll capture both. primary SLO will be measured server-side at time of first token emitted by model service (i.e., time from request acceptance to first token). secondary is end-to-end from browser to first render — we'll run synthetic e2e with your staging env to capture that delta.

[06:05] Ethan: measurement plan details:
- Synthetic inference run: single request latency distribution over 10k requests across warm and cold runs. Capture TTFT, TPOT (per token), and total response time.
- Concurrency run: step up concurrency from 1 -> 200 to find knee and tail behavior; capture 95/99 latencies and error rates.
- E2E run: replay traffic through your app stack with sample workload for 30-60 min to validate real-world latencies.
- Cache tests: cold start (empty KV), warm (after 1000 similar prompts), and prefix cache enabled.

[06:45] Rina: regarding TPOT, do you include tokenizer time? we run tok on client sometimes; want consistent measurement.
[06:52] Ethan: for server-side TPOT we'll measure model inference time including tokenization if it's done server-side; we'll annotate which side does tokenization. for client-side tok we'll provide a separate column.

[07:05] Luis: benchmarks need to show reproducible scripts. share runbook and we will run it on our staging to avoid hitting prod.
[07:12] Maya: yes, we'll provide scripts, and ether you or we can run to compare. we prefer running together so we can see metrics live.

[07:30] Ethan: instrumentation: we'll emit detailed logs including request_id, model_version, kernel_profile, batch_size, seq_len, TTFT_ms, TPOT_ms, total_ms. then aggregate histograms for p50/p95/p99. note histograms are more helpful for tail.

[07:55] Ben: curious about batching — you mentioned continuous batching earlier; does that impact TTFT?
[08:00] Ethan: continuous batching optimizes throughput but can add micro-batching delays; for strict TTFT targets we'll run with batching minimized. however for TPOT and cost tests we'll run with batching enabled to show tradeoffs.

[08:20] Rina: can we test quantized models? we plan to try int8. how much does that change TPOT?
[08:27] Ethan: int8 typically reduces TPOT by 20-40% depending on kernelization and model; we'll include both fp16 and int8 runs.

[08:40] Luis: timeline — we're hoping to have a decision in 3 weeks. what is realistic for the POC run?
[08:47] Maya: if we get sample traffic and access this week, we can scope and size, deliver a proposal by 10/07, run baseline benchmarks week of 10/11, and have results by 10/15. that aligns with a 3-week decision window.

[09:05] Ethan: dependencies: network access (whitelist ips), sample prompts, a staging endpoint, and a contact to run the e2e. also confirm any compliance docs needed for the POC.

[09:20] Rina: we'll need SOC2 and encryption details — our security team will review.

[09:25] Maya: i'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper in the follow-up.

[09:38] Luis: curious about cost — show us tradeoff of latency vs cost per 1k tokens for different configs.
[09:45] Ethan: yes, as part of 'redwood optimize' we'll include estimated cost per token across quantization and batch settings, and show the sweet spot where latency SLOs are met at lowest cost.

[10:02] Ben: error handling and fallbacks — if p99 spikes, do you offer automatic fallback?
[10:08] Maya: yes, we can configure routing policies and automatic fallback to smaller model variants or other regions; for POC we'll test fallback behavior as part of resilience tests.

[10:22] Ethan: measurement specifics for SLO calc: we'll calculate p95/p99 on server-side TTFT for all successful requests over a sliding 5-minute window, and declare pass if the observed p95 <= target and p99 <= target for the 5-minute peak window. throughput SLO measured as sustained rps over same window with p95 TTFT meeting target.

[10:55] Rina: sounds good. small nit: sliding window and how many samples required? we need statistical significance.

[11:02] Ethan: we'll require a minimum of 1k requests in the window for p95/p99 to count; otherwise we mark as inconclusive. we'll include confidence intervals in the report.

[11:18] Luis: do you provide raw logs/metrics to ingest into our prometheus/grafana?

[11:25] Maya: yes we can stream metrics to your prometheus via pushgateway or provide csv exports.

[11:35] Rina: ok next steps recap pls.

[11:40] Maya: recap — we'll send proposal + sizing (Maya), ethan will share benchmark runbook, rina to provide prompts and traffic, ben to set up network access. schedule baseline run week of 10/11.

[11:55] Luis: thanks, please call out the exact SLOs in the proposal.

[12:00] Maya: will do, we'll list test matrix, infra configs, and acceptance criteria.

[12:10] Ethan: any other technical questions?

[12:15] Ben: only one — latency measurement under TLS termination might add 10-20ms, factor that in.

[12:20] Ethan: we'll show both TLS and internal timings.

[12:30] (wrap) Maya: thanks everyone, will follow up with docs and proposal.


Notes / Measurement plan bullets (captured in call):
- Define TTFT (server-side): request-accept -> first token emitted; include tokenization note.
- Define TPOT: average ms per token during generation phase; report p95/p99.
- Success criteria (POC): TTFT p95 <= 350ms; TTFT p99 <= 700ms; TPOT p95 <= 60ms; throughput: sustain 20 rps during 5-min peak with p95 TTFT target.
- Measurement methodology: synthetic inference-only 10k requests (warm/cold), concurrency ramp 1->200, e2e replay 30-60m, cache/cold/warm scenarios, quantization matrix (fp16,int8).
- Aggregation rules: server-side histograms, require min 1k samples per window, sliding 5-min windows for SLO evaluation, include confidence intervals.
- Fallback/resilience: test automatic model fallback to smaller variant and measure SLO delta.

Artifacts to be shared: POC proposal (doc), sizing worksheet (spreadsheet), benchmark runbook (scripts + config), security whitepaper, SOC2 cert, sample traffic profile.

End of transcript.
